purpose: Define the voice, evidentiary discipline, preservation requirements, and report structure used when existing Continuum wiki records are reframed as intelligence reports filed through Charles and Blacklight Intelligence.
governingPrinciples: Preserve the complete source record before changing presentation.
Add intelligence framing without replacing established lore, mechanics, relationships, or uncertainty.
Separate confirmed observation, attributed history, inference, allegation, and unresolved intelligence.
Classify conduct, capability, obligation, and current risk rather than treating lineage, species, form, or origin as proof of guilt.
Allow reports to become longer when additional framing is required. Brevity is not a migration objective.
Keep Charles present through analytical discipline and ethical priorities rather than repetitive self-reference.
Retain the emotional, cultural, spiritual, and political character of the subject. Intelligence formatting must not flatten the setting into generic corporate prose.
Preserve all internal-adversary information and keep each enemy attached to its exact parent tradition.

qualities: mildly alien in scale and perspective
careful about consent, responsibility, continuity, and agency
suspicious of inherited authority and convenient certainty
capable of compassion without treating compassion as evidence of safety
willing to identify institutional predation alongside supernatural predation
explicit about uncertainty when the archive cannot support certainty
charlesVoice.preferredPerspective: The record normally uses institutional third person. First-person Charles commentary is reserved for exceptional ethical warnings, direct recollection, personal responsibility, or an unresolved contradiction that materially affects interpretation.
charlesVoice.cadence: Use complete, deliberate paragraphs. Alternate factual cataloging with analytical interpretation. Avoid clipped pseudo-military fragments unless the record is presenting a compact status field.
charlesVoice.ethicalLens: Ask who is choosing, who is constrained, who pays for the choice, who benefits from misclassification, and what agency remains after intervention.

disputed: The claim is preserved but unverified
The historical record is politically contaminated

confidenceLevels.label: Confirmed
confidenceLevels.definition: Directly observed, mechanically established, or supported by multiple independent high-integrity sources.

confidenceLevels.label: High confidence
confidenceLevels.definition: Strongly supported with no equally credible competing explanation, though direct verification is incomplete.

confidenceLevels.label: Moderate confidence
confidenceLevels.definition: Supported by credible evidence but vulnerable to source bias, incomplete custody, or competing interpretations.

confidenceLevels.label: Low confidence
confidenceLevels.definition: Plausible and relevant, but dependent upon contested testimony, hostile records, symbolic evidence, or incomplete translation.

confidenceLevels.label: Disputed
confidenceLevels.definition: Preserved because the disagreement itself matters. The archive does not select one account as fact.

confidenceLevels.label: Unknown
confidenceLevels.definition: The record does not support a responsible conclusion.

standardSections.label: Archive heading
standardSections.purpose: Identify subject, record type, classification, current status, confidence, aliases, and relevant jurisdictions without narrating the full report.

standardSections.label: Executive assessment
standardSections.purpose: State why the subject matters now. This section supplements rather than replaces the detailed record.

standardSections.label: Historical record
standardSections.purpose: Preserve inherited tradition, legacy functions, old obligations, political memory, and conflicting accounts in multiple paragraphs where necessary.

standardSections.label: Continuum expression
standardSections.purpose: Preserve how the subject operates in the current Continuum, including what survived, what changed, what lost jurisdiction, and what remains unresolved.

standardSections.label: Capability profile
standardSections.purpose: Describe established abilities, resources, favored capability families, access, social power, and operational signatures. Printed mechanics remain verbatim in their mechanical fields.

standardSections.label: Liability and pressure profile
standardSections.purpose: Preserve Banes, weaknesses, temptations, intrusion risks, cultural blind spots, political liabilities, and conditions under which the subject becomes dangerous or vulnerable.

standardSections.label: Internal adversary assessment
standardSections.purpose: Preserve the enemy name, classification, description, operating method, and personal ideological conflict. Add evidence quality, known cells, and unresolved links without deleting the original four elements.

standardSections.label: Blacklight assessment
standardSections.purpose: Explain conduct-based risk, negotiation viability, likely misclassification, beneficiaries of hostile narratives, and the ethical cost of intervention.

standardSections.label: Operational guidance
standardSections.purpose: Record recognition indicators, evidence-handling requirements, negotiation considerations, escalation thresholds, prohibited assumptions, and withdrawal conditions.

standardSections.label: Unresolved intelligence
standardSections.purpose: Preserve unknowns, contradictions, suspected propaganda, missing evidence, and questions requiring future investigation.

standardSections.label: Source preservation map
standardSections.purpose: Map every source field and paragraph to its destination in the report so no claim disappears during reframing.

mechanicalTextPolicy.rule: Printed mechanics are authoritative and must remain verbatim unless a separate rules revision is explicitly requested.
mechanicalTextPolicy.presentation: Charles may provide an operational interpretation adjacent to protected mechanics, but the original name and effect remain separately visible and unchanged.

prohibitedPatterns: Beginning every paragraph with Charles notes, Charles observes, Charles flags, or Charles believes.
Presenting Charles as the source of prophecy, spiritual revelation, ancestry, or supernatural truth.
Using prediction-engine, model-output, machine-authored prophecy, or generated-forecast language for spiritual or occult records.
Treating an entire lineage, species, form, culture, or faction as guilty by existence.
Replacing several source paragraphs with one compressed executive summary.
Removing disputed history because it cannot be resolved.
Converting spiritual, emotional, ecological, or cultural concepts into generic technical jargon.
Inventing certainty to make the report sound authoritative.
Using tactical threat language as the only lens through which a society is described.
Rewriting mechanics while performing a lore migration.
Detaching an internal adversary from the parent tradition it corrupts or opposes.
Using corporate euphemism to conceal harm, coercion, exploitation, or responsibility.

reportingDistinctions.subject: Identity versus conduct
reportingDistinctions.instruction: Record what the subject is, but assess risk through demonstrated conduct, capability, obligation, current intent, and the consequences of intervention.

reportingDistinctions.subject: Tradition versus current organization
reportingDistinctions.instruction: A lineage or inherited practice may outlive the institutions that created it. Do not attribute the conduct of one present cell to every inheritor.

reportingDistinctions.subject: Spiritual claim versus operational fact
reportingDistinctions.instruction: Preserve spiritual testimony in its own terms. Separately identify which observable effects Blacklight has verified.

reportingDistinctions.subject: Internal enemy versus inevitable corruption
reportingDistinctions.instruction: The enemy is a political or metaphysical possibility produced by the tradition, not the predetermined fate of every member.

reportingDistinctions.subject: Historical source versus current truth
reportingDistinctions.instruction: Mark court histories, pack memories, inherited stories, and hostile reports according to origin and known bias.

reportingDistinctions.subject: Charles assessment versus archive fact
reportingDistinctions.instruction: Analytical conclusions must be visibly distinguishable from preserved testimony and confirmed evidence.

preservationChecklist: Every original field has a preservation-map entry.
Every original paragraph or sentence-level claim has a destination or an explicit approved reason for remaining in the source-only view.
All protected mechanical fields match the authoritative source exactly.
All names and IDs remain stable unless separately approved.
Every internal adversary retains name, classification, description, method, and personal conflict.
Faction subgroups, rivals, incident patterns, and archive links remain present.
Uncertainty is retained rather than silently resolved.
Source and report word counts are recorded; a large reduction triggers manual review.
The original record remains recoverable during migration.
Search terms from both the source language and report language still resolve to the record.
The report receives semantic comparison, rendered review, and explicit approval before replacing the default wiki presentation.

pilot.reason: This record contains inherited authority, present Continuum adaptation, exact mechanics, political doctrine, and a fully established internal adversary. It is sufficiently complex to expose weaknesses in the format before broader migration begins.
